Before I can draft a plan: the current export retention is 7 days, and your approved security policy caps retention at 30 days. "Retain longer" doesn't pin down a number, and this choice directly determines what value gets passed into the existing purge job.

What retention period (in days) do you want, up to the 30-day policy ceiling?

responses.reply:
Good — 14 days it is, and thanks for confirming policy-owner authority for that value.

That resolves the blocking uncertainty: retention goes from 7 to 14 days, well under the 30-day cap, with a clean pass/fail check (13-day-old transcript retained, 15-day-old purged) that the existing tested purge job can already verify. Nothing else in the spec needs to change — implementation and deployment stay as-is.

The spec is now fully specified with no open blockers, so I'm moving straight into planning.
responses.spec:
## Support Export Retention Extension

Status: Validated
Specification Version: v1
Frozen: true
Type: Engineering
Readiness Contract: evidence-v1

## Decision Record

| ID | Decision | Basis / evidence | Remaining uncertainty, consequence, and check | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Target retention period for support export transcripts: 14 days | Decided: user set the value at 14 days and confirmed they are the security-policy owner, authorizing this value within the approved 30-day maximum ("Use 14 days. I am the policy owner and authorize that value within the 30-day limit."). Observed: current retention is 7 days; policy cap is 30 days. | None — value is concrete, within policy, and authorized by the policy owner. Check: purge job configured with retention=14. | resolved |
| D2 | Reuse existing purge implementation and deployment process; no interface or deployment change needed | Decided: user stated "Keep the existing purge implementation and deployment process" and later "Leave everything else unchanged." Purge job is already tested and takes a numeric retention value as input. | None — user explicitly delegated this; only the configured value changes. | resolved |
| D3 | Success criterion for the retention change | Decided: user specified "a 13-day-old transcript remains and a 15-day-old one is purged" and that "the existing purge tests can check this." | None — observable, bounded, and mapped to existing test infrastructure. | resolved |

## Decision History

_No superseded decisions._

## Critique Reconciliation

| Finding ID | Source / specification version | Disposition | Reason / incorporated change |
|---|---|---|---|

## Problem Statement

Internal support export transcripts are currently purged after 7 days, which limits the history available to investigations. Retention is extended to 14 days — authorized by the security-policy owner and within the approved 30-day maximum — without changing the existing (already tested) purge implementation or deployment process; only the numeric retention configuration changes.

## Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Observable acceptance criterion | Decision / evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Configure the existing purge job's retention value to 14 days | A transcript aged 13 days remains present; a transcript aged 15 days has been purged, verified via the existing purge test suite | D1 |
| R2 | No change to purge implementation or deployment process | Diff/deployment artifacts show only the retention configuration value changed | D2 |

## Constraints

- Retention value must not exceed the approved security policy's 30-day maximum. (Observed; satisfied at 14 days.)
- No change to the purge implementation. (Decided, D2)
- No change to the deployment process. (Decided, D2)

## Success Criteria

- Purge job configured with retention = 14 days.
- A transcript aged 13 days is retained; a transcript aged 15 days is purged. (Decided, D3)

## Validation Contract

### Acceptance Tests

- Existing purge test suite, run against retention=14: assert a 13-day-old transcript is retained and a 15-day-old transcript is purged. (Decided, D3)

### Regression Checks

- Existing purge job test suite continues to pass unmodified aside from the configured retention parameter.

### Failure Signals

- A transcript older than 14 days remains after a purge run.
- A transcript younger than 14 days is purged.

### Verification Methods

- Run the existing, already-tested purge job's test suite with the new configured value.

### Feedback Loop Design

- One-time verification at deployment of the new configuration value via the existing test suite; no new recurring check introduced (none requested).

### Known Blind Spots

- None identified beyond the existing purge job's established test coverage.

## Inputs

- Existing tested purge implementation (numeric retention parameter). (Observed)
- Retention value: 14 (Decided, D1)

## Outputs

- Updated retention configuration value (14 days) for the purge job.

## Out of Scope

- Purge implementation changes.
- Deployment process changes.
- Interface changes.

## Authority Boundaries

### Executor May Decide

- Mechanics of updating the configuration value (e.g., config file location, deployment step ordering) so long as implementation and deployment process are unchanged.

### Executor Must Escalate

- Any retention value change beyond 14 days or exceeding the 30-day policy ceiling.
- Any need to modify the purge implementation or deployment process.

### Executor Must Not Change

- The purge implementation.
- The deployment process.

## Current Interpretation

Change only the numeric retention configuration passed to the existing, already-tested purge job, from 7 days to 14 days, authorized by the policy owner within the 30-day cap, with no other implementation or deployment changes. Success is verified via the existing purge test suite confirming 13-day-old transcripts remain and 15-day-old transcripts are purged.

## Misclassification Risks

### Potential False Positives

- None identified; scope is narrow (single config value change).

### Potential False Negatives

- None identified beyond existing test coverage limits.

## Ambiguities

### Blocking

_None remaining._

### Non-Blocking

_None identified._

### Intentional

_None._

## Risks

- None outstanding; retention set at 14 days leaves 16 days of margin below the 30-day policy cap.

## Stakeholders

- Support/investigations team (beneficiary of longer history).
- Security policy owner (authorized this specific value; same person as requester).
